name: Burundi

findings.financier: China Eximbank (buyer's credit; African Trade Insurance guarantee)
findings.summary: A China Eximbank buyer's credit of about US$7.9m, signed in 2004, paid for Huawei to expand Onatel's GSM mobile network from 30,000 to 60,000 lines in three phases, starting in Bujumbura; all phases were reported complete in November 2014.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary) Chinese Development Finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: Huawei as equipment vendor under the service contract, so prc. AidData is a research dataset compiled from official and press sources; coded S2. US$7.91m is the loan amount, not a verified contract figure. Whether Onatel's mobile network still runs this Huawei equipment was not checked; a 2017 report says it had not been upgraded since 2009-2010 (see BDI-004).

findings.local_actor: Government of Burundi; Onatel (operator after handover)
findings.financier: China Eximbank (concessional loan per AidData; press described Chinese government funding as a grant or loan)
findings.summary: Huawei built a roughly 220 km fibre Metropolitan Area Network in Bujumbura linking the presidency, parliament, courts, hospitals and ministries; construction began October 2014 and the network was handed to Onatel in December 2016.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary) Chinese Development Finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: Huawei as builder and equipment vendor of a government network, so prc. Financing is inconsistent across sources: DCD and PC Tech say a Chinese government grant, Iwacu a Chinese loan, AidData a US$14.98m China Eximbank loan (1%, 28 years); value recorded is that loan. PC Tech coded S4 as it leans on Huawei statements. Current operation not confirmed.

findings.summary: ZTE reportedly won the tender to lay about 1,300 km of national fibre backbone for Burundi, a roughly US$10.5m World Bank grant-funded project, with a first phase expected in early 2012.
findings.analyst_inference: ZTE as fibre and equipment contractor, so prc under the equipment-vendor rule, although the backbone is owned by the BBS operator consortium. Single opened source, so low confidence. A ZTE corporate release on an IT infrastructure agreement with BBS appeared in search but was not fetched or cited (PRC vendor site). Completion and current vendor not confirmed. Pre-2020.

findings.controller: Huawei International (lender; equipment vendor not named)
findings.summary: Burundi's government announced plans to modernise and extend the state operator's mobile network, unchanged since 2009-2010, financed by a US$30m loan from Huawei International repayable over ten years.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole left null: the source names Huawei only as lender, not as equipment supplier. Vendor financing of this kind usually comes with Huawei equipment (analyst inference), which would make it prc. Tier 1 as a government announcement; whether the loan closed or the upgrade was delivered was not found. Pre-2020.

findings.builder: China National Electronics Import & Export Corporation (CEIEC) (named implementer)
findings.summary: China pledged to build a 'Big Data Center' for Burundi under a grant-based economic and technical cooperation agreement, with CEIEC named as implementer; AidData records no funding figure and says construction had not begun.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary) Chinese Development Finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: Pole domestic on the assumption the government would own and operate the centre; CEIEC as builder. Tier 1 pledge only. AidData's 'not started' status reflects its data cut-off, not the run date, so still_current is null. Whether a national data centre was later built, and by whom, is unknown.

silicon.null_reason: no accelerator purchases or deployments surfaced in any of the run's searches; no dedicated search spent given Burundi's market size

models.null_reason: one search found Burundi validated a national AI strategy (reported April 2026; a UNDP page on the roadmap appeared in search results only) but no named frontier-model provider partnership or government model adoption

applications.null_reason: two searches (English and French) found no reporting of a safe-city or CCTV system in Bujumbura or a named surveillance vendor

power.null_reason: no AI- or data-centre-specific power evidence surfaced

research_gaps: RAN and core vendors of Lumitel (Viettel), Econet Leo and Onatel today; Lumitel's 2016-2018 4G rollout reporting names no equipment vendor.
